  "concordance_definition": "The paper states that the ZeGlobalTox assay achieves high toxicity predictivity with specificity (89%), sensitivity (68%), and accuracy (78%) when comparing zebrafish experimental data with known human toxicity outputs.",
  "limitations_stated": [
    "Cardiotoxic false negatives could be explained by differences among human and zebrafish physiology or by the ZeGlobalTox procedure, where cardiotoxic effects are analysed only 4 h after drug incubation, and some compounds might require a longer exposure.",
    "The experimental methodology for cardiotoxicity (drug exposure timing, chosen drug concentration, image acquisition, and image analysis) might require some further improvement to facilitate a more accurate detection of some of the analysed parameters.",
    "Locomotion results should be interpreted cautiously as drugs altering zebrafish locomotion could be neurotoxic, but also non-neurotoxic compounds affecting the function of the nervous system.",
    "Drugs not influencing larvae locomotion cannot be tagged safe for neurotoxicity, since they might be neurotoxic without affecting locomotor neural pathways.",
    "The exposure to NOEC might yield some false negatives.",
    "Testing more than one concentration might provide a better understanding of a possible drug-induced organ liability, if that phenotype requires a higher than NOEC concentration to be triggered."
  ],

    "10% of molecules entering phase 1 clinical trials are ultimately approved by the FDA",
    "24 compounds were evaluated in the ZeGlobalTox platform",
    "4 drugs were used as positive toxic controls",
